note: Policy gates mounted on an /api path production sends to the functions host, so each decides only for developer machines. `getApiUrl` rewrites /api/<seg> straight to functions.printyx.net, so Express answers a path only when nothing over there claims the segment. The AMBIENT stack (requireAuth, resolveTenant and friends) is exempt BY NAME in the script with its reason - the edge function authenticates and resolves tenancy itself, so an Express copy not running there is the architecture. Everything below is a policy decision, and the reason says whether the edge function carries an equivalent (redundant, keep) or does not (a gap, and which one). Shrink-only; an entry with no reason is refused. Added in round 120/LAUNCH-013 after this session found the same shape five times by hand - LAUNCH-010's auth rate limiters, AUDIT-034's IP whitelist and MFA gate, SEC-003's Helmet, and these.

accepted.server/routes-companies.ts::validate: Zod body validation on POST /api/companies/check-duplicate. Not a security gate, and recorded because the endpoint behind it is the real finding: supabase/functions/companies/ has NO check-duplicate branch, so that path 404s in production and only developers ever reach the handler this validates.
accepted.server/routes-crm-core.ts::enforceUsageL: LAUNCH-013's ONLY usage gate, on POST /api/leads. supabase/functions/leads/ serves that path in production and carries no subscription, plan or usage check - grep tenant_subscriptions across supabase/functions and only subscriptions/ and _shared/stripe.ts match. So plan limits are not enforced on record creation in production at all. A GAP, not redundancy.
accepted.server/routes-csv-import.ts::requirePerm: RBAC on /api/import/upload and /api/import/jobs/:jobId/execute. Covered edge-side: supabase/functions/import/index.ts carries two role checks, so the Express copy is redundant rather than load-bearing.
accepted.server/routes-csv-import.ts::requireFeat: The ai_csv_import plan feature flag on /api/import/ai/map-columns and /ai-process. supabase/functions/import/ has role checks but no feature or plan check, so the AI import paths are open to any tenant regardless of plan in production. A GAP, and LAUNCH-013's second half.
accepted.server/routes-product-models.ts::require: RBAC on seven /api/product-models paths. Covered edge-side: supabase/functions/product-models/ is gated on operations.inventory.manage (SEC-EDGE-001's catalogue family).
accepted.server/routes-products-crud.ts::can: RBAC on twenty paths across product-models, product-accessories, professional-services, supplies, inventory, managed-services and meter-readings. Six of the seven edge functions are gated (the catalogue family). meter-readings is the exception - zero gate calls in supabase/functions/meter-readings/ - so a meter write is ungated in production while the Express twin checks a permission nobody reaches.
accepted.server/routes-technician-management.ts::: RBAC on eight /api/technician-management paths. Covered edge-side since round 92, which found exactly this split by hand: all five edge writes were ungated while the Express copy checked SERVICE.TECHNICIAN.MANAGE, so dev was the safe host and production the open one. Eight gate calls in that function now.
accepted.server/routes.ts::csrfTokenLimiter: Rate limit on GET /api/csrf-token. supabase/functions/csrf-token/ is a headless edge function with no rate limit of its own, so the token endpoint is unthrottled in production. Low stakes - it mints a CSRF token and touches no tenant data - but the limiter is not doing what its name says on the host that matters.
